subject: Incorrect file permissions on log files with "user_dirs" enabled

messages.author: de4af37471a0f1bb
messages.subject: Incorrect file permissions on log files with "user_dirs" enabled
parts:
Hi,

We have Shiny Server up and running successfully but users are unable to debug their apps without Admin assistance.
The users are not able to read their app logs at ~/ShinyApps/log/ due to permission settings of 640.
Should the permissions not be set to '644' by Shiny when using "user_dirs"?

regards,

Drew

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: Incorrect file permissions on log files with "user_dirs" enabled
parts:
Hi Drew,

This is by design. Files are restricted to the owners of those applications. But we can look into making this more flexible/configurable.

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.subject: Re: Incorrect file permissions on log files with "user_dirs" enabled
parts:
Hi Fereshteh,

in this case, it IS the owner of the app who cannot see the logs! The logs are owned by "shiny", the server daemon user and are not world readable. Therefore the owner of the apps cannot read the logs to debug issues. We have also noticed that the logs "evaporate" when the session ends.

I have not been able to identify any relevant server settings to fix this, perhaps I am missing something in the Shiny server setup?

regards,

Drew

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: Incorrect file permissions on log files with "user_dirs" enabled
parts:
Hi Drew,

Oh, sorry for misunderstanding. 
If you are using "user_dirs" there are 2 options for how your R process runs: You can either have the R process to run as one single global user (such as "shiny") for all your applications, or have the R process to run as the owner of the application (based on the path to application). So it seems that you need the latter. For this you need to change your configuration file, and have the following:

run_as  :HOME_USER:;

With this, when you access  http://server/user1/app1 (just as an example) the R process will run as "user1" and the log file will be owned by "user1".

You can read more about this in the Admin Guide: http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#home_user

And as for the log files disappearing, this is the case when R process exits without error. If there are errors, we expect that the log file remains. 

Hope this helps.

Fereshteh
